title: Earth-Science Statistics Cheat Sheet
question: What is the statistical toolkit for environmental data, applied to real observations, with the assumptions, the reading of the output and the pitfalls written down?
one_liner: Runnable, annotated analysis scripts, each printing an interpretation of what it computed, condensed into a one-page method chooser.
aim: Document the statistical toolkit for environmental data as runnable, annotated examples on real observations, with assumptions, interpretation and failure modes stated for each method.
scope: Exploratory analysis, hypothesis tests, regression, time series, trend and change-point detection, extremes, resampling, multivariate and spatial methods, Bayesian estimation and machine learning, on NOAA, NASA GISTEMP, GHCN-Daily and USGS streamflow data.
conclusion: Runnable reference with generated worked-example results; no new scientific study is claimed.

summary.question: Worked examples of the statistics used on environmental data, each run on real observations with its assumptions and pitfalls written out.

finding: Each script applies one family of methods to real or clearly labelled synthetic data and prints an interpretation, so the output reads like a worked example. The cheat sheet is the index: a table from question to method to script section, with the assumptions and the failure modes beside each.

traps.how: Station-temperature interpolation uses leave-one-out validation with the trend and variograms fitted inside each fold. Transfer to an unsampled region requires a separate spatial holdout.
The hypothesis-test section covers multiple comparisons and false-discovery control.

figures.caption: Regression kriging and residual uncertainty; the station-elevation grid is approximate.
Residual variogram fitted to station climatologies.

not_claimed: A reference, not a study; no new empirical finding is claimed.
data: NOAA CO2, GISTEMP, GHCN-Daily, USGS streamflow and station climatologies
